description: Sánchez's opener: assistant flagged Ramsey offside but Taylor overruled him (Ramsey judged not interfering); Chelsea also claimed Sánchez handled in the build-up. BBC: Chelsea 'left nursing a serious sense of injustice'; Conte called the goal 'very strange'.

Phil Jones fouled Hazard for the penalty and was booked rather than sent off. BBC explainer: under the 2016 Law 12 change a DOGSO foul in the area that is an attempt to play the ball is a caution, so yellow was correct; BBC noted 'plenty of debate on social media'.

Moses' cut-back struck Ashley Young's forearm in the United area; penalty plea dismissed and VAR did not intervene. Shearer and Wright (BBC MOTD) said the referee was right not to use VAR as it was not 'clear and obvious'.
Doucouré's shot struck Vincent Kompany's arm in the City area; Friend (after VAR check per Wikipedia) gave no penalty and booked Doucouré for protesting.
Kovačić shown a second yellow for a challenge on Granit Xhaka. BBC (McNulty): 'very harshly sent off ... for the most innocuous of challenges'; questioned whether it was a foul at all.

Chelsea players claimed the ball hit Ayoze Pérez's hand in the build-up to Tielemans' goal; VAR did not intervene. Tuchel: 'The players said straight away it was a handball ... VAR is not interfering'; BBC noted 'a suspicion of handball before Tielemans' goal'.

VAR (Coote) intervened for a Jack Grealish handball from Wan-Bissaka's header; Fernandes scored. Grealish: 'I don't even think it's a penalty'. Dale Johnson: classic modern handball, arm moved up above shoulder, 'some referees will disagree' but a penalty is always likely with VAR.
Casemiro caught Manuel Akanji above the ankle; referee gave the free kick the wrong way (to United). VAR checked for a red; ESPN: yellow-worthy but not a definite red, so no intervention possible.

Kevin De Bruyne went down under a challenge from Fred; Tierney waved play on and VAR had a lengthy check without intervening. ESPN: 'a stronger claim' than a comparable incident, but did not reach the clear-and-obvious threshold.
Haaland appeared to be bundled over by Lisandro Martínez from Bernardo Silva's cross; Madley waved away 'huge' City appeals and VAR checked without a review. Sky: 'the game's first huge flashpoint'.

Dean Henderson, standing in his area, handled the ball outside the area to stop Erling Haaland running onto Gvardiol's long ball. No free kick; VAR (Gillett) checked for DOGSO and did not intervene, judging the chance not obvious as the ball was going away from goal. Guardiola: 'Ask the referee'.
Tyrick Mitchell's sliding challenge on Bernardo Silva: penalty given and upheld by VAR despite Mitchell touching the ball; Marmoush's kick saved by Henderson.
Enzo Fernández's heavy challenge on Bernardo Silva (foot off the ground) drew a yellow; City's bench including Guardiola called for red. BBC reporter: 'Lucky to get just a yellow...?'
Joao Pedro burst into the box and came together with Abdukodir Khusanov; no penalty, VAR (Bankes) checked and did not recommend a review.
Jorrel Hato went down after a collision with Khusanov; referee waved play on and VAR did not intervene. Interim coach McFarlane: 'for me, it's a clear penalty'.

Arsenal claimed Agüero fouled (pushed) Shkodran Mustafi in the build-up to the opening goal; Pawson allowed it and VAR was satisfied. Wilshere said 'it is a foul'; Wenger conceded there was no 'obvious' push.
Kompany's goal: Arsenal (Wenger '100 per cent offside', Wilshere) argued Leroy Sané was offside and interfering; goal stood.
Wilshere said a City player should have received a second yellow card in the first half (player not named in the report; Fernandinho, booked 36', is the only City player booked in the first half).

Corner from which Rodri headed City's second goal: Sky's report calls it 'contentiously-awarded'; the Irish Times report questions whether the corner should have been given, as the last touch 'seemed to be off Gundogan rather than Grealish'.

Laporte fouled Lucas Moura twice to stop counter-attacks (c.24', not booked; just before half-time, booked). Sky's report says he was 'perhaps lucky only to be booked' for the second; Tottenham's official report notes Tierney did not book the first foul, meaning the second could otherwise have been a second yellow/red. Laporte scored the 82' winner.

Joel Matip's header from a free-kick routine (Mané headed across) ruled out after referee Stuart Attwell was sent to the monitor by VAR Darren England: Virgil van Dijk, starting from an offside position, was judged to have impeded Reece James.
Naby Keïta's high challenge on Trevoh Chalobah (caught in the groin area) - no card. Covered in Sky's Ref Watch.

Van Dijk headed in Robertson's free-kick; after a lengthy check VAR John Brooks sent referee Chris Kavanagh to the monitor and the goal was ruled out because Wataru Endo, in an offside position, blocked Levi Colwill from challenging.
First-half challenge by Moisés Caicedo on Ryan Gravenberch's ankle; Gravenberch stretchered off. No card, no VAR intervention; Klopp reported furious.

Van Nistelrooy's drive appeared to be blocked by Henchoz's arm about a minute after Carragher came on (83'); no penalty. Second of the two Henchoz handball appeals cited by the Irish Examiner as 'seemingly clear-cut'.

Minamino's equaliser came after his pass rebounded off Mohamed Salah; Arsenal protested a Salah handball. VAR checked quickly; BBC said replay showed no clear contact, ESPN said VAR replays showed no obvious foul play.

Nathan Aké tripped/kicked out at Iheanacho in the box; Tierney gave the penalty. Fernandinho argued so strongly (that the contact was not a foul) that he was booked (Mail on Sunday). BBC simply reports Iheanacho was 'tripped by Nathan Ake'.

Núñez's header struck Rúben Dias's arm; Pawson initially waved play on, then after VAR (John Brooks) advised a monitor review he awarded a penalty, converted by Salah. Former City defender Nedum Onuoha questioned the decision, arguing the ball was headed onto the arm.
Álvarez's equaliser was initially flagged offside but awarded after a lengthy VAR check (overturned).

Under the new 2023-24 added-time directive, 8 minutes of stoppage time were extended (to ~13-14) after a Walker-Partey head clash; Trossard equalised in the 101st minute. Guardiola questioned the new injury-time rules afterwards; Arteta disagreed.
